title: Cut slow athena-cli test binaries' time using test-only changes
summary: Retry of the test-suite speedup: reduce `cargo test --locked` wall time to under 6 minutes by changing only test code and fixtures (athena-cli tests lifecycle, job_plan, drain, retry, steward and common/mod.rs). Production source (secrets.rs, checks.rs) stays untouched. Audience: the user, who reads docs/decisions.md and later job times.

defaults_applied.how: All changes are Rust test code.
cargo test, clippy and fmt must pass.
Decision cites measured timings and labels estimates.
Criteria require running cargo test and checking time and pass.
Limited to the slowest test binaries and the docs.
Find the cause per binary before cutting.
Outcome is measured wall time under 6 minutes.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Nextest is rejected (584 s vs 673 s, about 13%); no new tool, athena.toml, or ci.yml change.
Baseline measured by the brain: compile 67 s, run 673 s on 4 cores; per-binary: lifecycle 174 s, job_plan 83 s, drain 61 s, athena-core unit 61 s, retry 54 s, steward 48 s, introspection 36 s.
The last attempt got the run to about 405 s of test time using production edits; test-only edits may reach less, so the producer should time each binary first and prioritize by saving per effort.
Production code may change only by a test-only hook (cfg(test) or env/parameter override used by tests) with production defaults unchanged.
If the 6-minute target cannot be reached by test-only means, the decision records measured before and after times honestly instead of claiming it.

acceptance_criteria.text: docs/decisions.md has a new decision with per-binary before and after times (measured in the job, measured the same way for both, labeled as measured) for athena-cli lifecycle, job_plan, drain, retry and steward tests, and the cause found for each.

The decision records compile 67 s versus run 673 s (brain-measured) and lists cargo-nextest 0.9.148 (584 s vs 673 s) as rejected, with sccache per D79 and a shared target dir as considered alternatives; no unmeasured number is claimed.

git diff shows no change to crates/athena-gate/src/secrets.rs, crates/athena-core/src/checks.rs, athena.toml, ci.yml or tool pins; production default behavior is unchanged, and any production edit is only a test-only override. CHANGELOG.md has an entry.
No test is deleted, ignored or has its assertions weakened; the test count is not lower than before.
Run `cargo test --locked`: it passes with every test running and total test run time under 6 minutes, and a failing test still fails the run.
Run `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all --check`: both clean.

out_of_scope: Adopting cargo-nextest or any new pinned tool
Changing athena.toml, ci.yml, or sccache setup
Deleting, ignoring or weakening any test
departures: Higher cost and time than the reference: the producer must time and rework five slow test binaries, and the verifier reruns a roughly 6 to 10 minute suite. Pass odds are lower because the 6-minute target may not be reachable by test-only means (the last attempt reached about 405 s using production edits).
urgent_reason: This cuts wasted time: the 9.7-minute median check plus a producer rerun on every job, and the prior attempt was rejected for out-of-scope production edits.
